body:
Three shapes of test in this repo are structurally incapable of catching the
defect sitting next to them. Each one looks like coverage, reads like a
contract, and stays green through the bug it appears to guard. All three were
found in one night's work on the question-presentation surfaces, each beside a
real defect, and in every case the test was doing exactly what its name
promised.

This is written as a review question, not a proposal for a lint rule. See the
last section for why.

## 1. A test that pins a string

It asserts what a surface SAYS, word for word, and never asks what the surface
DOES. The assertion and the defect never meet.

Example. `internal/tui3/place_tasks_test.go:45`
`TestTheTasksFootIsScreenOneEWordForWord` pins the tasks page footer exactly.
Three more pin the same foot: `:91`, `:129`, `:204`. All four pass while the
page answers landings with digit keys that the footer never names, which breaks
the page's own law that nothing bound goes unnamed.

What the replacement asserts: press every key the page binds and assert the
footer names it, and press the keys the footer names and assert they do
something. A string test is fine as a companion to that and is not a substitute
for it.

## 2. A test that compares two booleans

It asserts that two readings AGREE and never that either is RIGHT. Both sides
can be wrong together, and the test stays green while they are.

Example. `internal/session/attach_test.go:433`
`TestNeedsPersonAgreesWithPresence` walks the lanes and pins that the agent's
`NeedsPerson()` agrees with the presence file's boolean. It never asserts that
the accompanying reason is non-empty, so it passes for a lane that says a person
is needed and says nothing about what for. That is a mark a person cannot act
on, and it survived because the only test in the area compares two booleans to
each other.

What the replacement asserts: the CONTENT each side carries, not their
agreement. For this case, that every lane which sets the boolean also produces a
sentence, and that the sentence names that lane's own question.

## 3. A test that pins one side of a pair

Two readers describe the same state and only one of them is pinned. The unpinned
side drifts, and nothing goes red.

Example. A landed task whose acceptance is still merging is described by two
readers. The record card at `internal/session/question.go:2987` says the person
already answered. The line home at `internal/session/taskpresence.go:1004` still
says `your call`, because it reads `PendingDecisions`, which filters on node
state alone. The card side is pinned five times in
`internal/session/questionlifecycle_test.go`, at `:254`, `:297`, `:328`, `:354`
and `:405`. The home side is pinned zero times. Five to nothing.

What the replacement asserts: both readers of one state, in one test, agreeing
about that state. This shape is the most useful of the three because it is
COUNTABLE. Count the tests per side before believing a pair is covered.

## The same family outside tests

Two more instances of the same shape were seen the same day in tooling rather
than in tests: a formatting check whose command exits zero whether or not it
found anything, and a summary line that reports only the last command in a
chain, so an earlier failure is invisible. A check whose failure mode cannot
appear is worse than no check, because it spends the attention a real check
would have earned.

## Why this is not a lint rule

None of the three is reliably detectable from source. A rule that caught a third
of them would restart exactly the same false comfort one level up, which is the
disease rather than the cure.

The review question instead, to ask of any test that looks like coverage:

**What would have to be broken for this test to fail? If the answer does not
include the defect it sits next to, it is not covering that defect.**

Three follow-ups that catch most of it in practice:

1. Does it assert what a surface says, or what it does?
2. Does it assert that two things agree, or that either one is right?
3. If two readers describe one state, how many tests does each side have?
